newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher, near day's peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher, near day's peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures edged up in afternoon trading and finished the day higher amid moderate trade.
Traders said a Fed coupon pass and the Fed's latest beige book report propped up debt futures after midday. Technical momentum propelled most contracts to fresh daily peaks late, traders said.
"We're still within the range but we tested the upside of it," a T-bond futures trader said.
September Treasury bonds rose to 112-8/32 in late trading, just shy of the four-month high set Tuesday at 112-10/32.

The Fed's "beige book" summary of the economy said the U.S. economy had expanded in May and early June, but showed some pockets of weakness. It also said labor markets tightened but there was little or no wage pressure.
September T-bonds immediately upticked after the report, and continued to drift up into the close.

Early in the session, September had matched Tuesday's 111-17/32 session low. Several technicians had said the market appeared to be blowing off steam after Tuesday's run to a four-month high. But September proved resilient, and rejected the Tuesday low.
Key support at 111-16/32 was unchallenged, with many holding upside targets near the February high of 113-9/32.

Some pegged resistance at Tuesday's high of 112-10/32, at 112-14/32, and at 112-27/32. Further support was at 110-23/32, a 38.2-percent retracement level from the contract's rally to 112-10/32 from 108-05/32.
"We had a lot of institutional paper buying size," a Treasury bond futures trader said. He said five companies late in the day bought up to 1,000 September contracts each.
December Euros also matched Tuesday's low, at 93.915, and extended gains into the close, traders noted.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 9/32 at 112-5/32, notes rose 4/32 to 109-2/32, and December Eurodollars were up 0.010 at 93.960. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
